5 ## Operating mode (standing, set 2026-06-28)
6 
7 - **Human-summaries only.** Replies are conclusions, not command/output transcripts.
8   Grunt work is routed through background sub-agents (isolated context → summary
9   only) so John's main view stays clean.
10 - **Control model (set 2026-06-28): Claude orchestrates + verifies; Gemini bulk-builds
11   under Claude's bounded dispatch.** Claude is the single controller — it owns the work
12   order, dispatches **discrete, capped** build tasks to Gemini via the `agy` CLI (one-shot
13   per call; never a free-running autonomous Gemini session), supervises concurrency so
14   there is **no uncapped swarm**, and does the **verification with Claude** tokens. Rationale:
15   Gemini does the heavy/voluminous building (cheaper tokens); Claude spends its tokens on
16   the lighter orchestration + cross-verification. Either side's GREEN still requires the
17   OTHER model to reproduce the gate (PLAN.md §6); verdicts logged to §7.
18 - **Swarm safety (hard rule).** Before/after dispatching workers, Claude checks for
19   orphaned `claude -p` / `agy` / stuck `pytest` process trees and reaps them. No spawn path
20   runs uncapped. (The 2026-06-27 crash and a 9h/14-zombie stuck-pytest on 2026-06-28 were
21   both this failure mode.)
22 - **No background process pops a console window** (claude or gemini): `windowsHide`,
23   `shell:false`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Enforced in every spawn.
24 - **Either model can drive; the other verifies — see [`HANDOFF.md`](./HANDOFF.md).**
25   It carries the role-swap mechanics (transports: `agy` for Gemini, `claude` for Claude)
26   so John can hand the wheel to Gemini when the Claude window gets full. **Whoever is
27   driving keeps HANDOFF.md §5 (current focus) + §6 (next steps) current** at the end of
28   every chunk, alongside PLAN.md §3/§7.

64 **Latest/highest model policy (John-approved 2026-09-08; formal Foundry improvement).**
65 All production seats, regular and Heavy, request `latest_supported` / `highest_supported` from the installed subscription CLI's current capability catalog or verified moving frontier alias. This supersedes one-notch-below defaults and per-project model pins. Exact IDs belong in discovery caches and run receipts, not durable preferences or tier tables. Highest effort is provider-specific; use Ultra when supported by the selected ChatGPT model, never pass that spelling blindly to another provider.
66 
67 Heavy remains a depth/stakes signal and triggers the existing independent-check policy; it does not license an older model for ordinary calls. Task depth, tool permissions and review independence remain separate from model quality. A base session cannot change its own model: use the resolved subscription seat for required delegated work and stamp actual service honestly. Explicit subagent defaults must match the resolved model/effort unless the isolation contract disables delegation, which must be disclosed.
68 
69 **Cross-model is a foundry-skill property — always AVAILABLE, fired by the STAKES GATE (amended 2026-07-11,
70 John-approved; family-prefs 2026-07-21).** Every foundry skill carries the true cross-model swarm
71 (**coding_family generates/codes, review_family independently checks**), and WHEN it fires is pre-decided —
72 never deliberated per run:
73 - **Fires:** stakes ≥ medium (the skill's own triage), ANY `-Heavy` run, or on John's request — **and**
74   coding_family ≠ review_family.
75 - **Skipped / single-family:** light regular-tier asks, **or** coding_family == review_family — honestly stamped
76   `cross_model:false` / degraded — the stamps exist precisely so a skipped or same-family check is VISIBLE,
77   never hidden.
78 Rationale: the always-on rule taxed every quick ask with cross-family latency the skills' own internal gates
79 would have skipped (2026-07-11 portfolio review, finding F4). The tier only swaps WHICH notch of the coding
80 family fills the coding seat. A single-family result is never passed off as cross-model, and a first `-Heavy`
81 run per skill must FORCE the cross-model seams when families differ (don't accept a host's default
82 single-family pick that contradicts prefs).
83 
84 **Trio BUILD tier (HEAVY vs STANDARD).** Preserve workflow depth and verification controls, but both use the shared latest/highest policy. `TRIO_TIER`, old `TRIO_MODEL_*` variables and per-project model names cannot override saved family choices or model policy. Capability discovery failure is explicit. Failover is bounded to configured families, journaled before launch, never silently replays ambiguous actions, and never turns verification into unmarked self-review.

116 ### Research reports for John — findings before process (2026-09-08)
117 
118 Applies to researchPrime, Literature-Review, Ramanujan and Jumper human-facing plans and results. Lead the results with an accessible executive summary: the main findings, what is already known, what might be a contribution, and what proof or experiment would establish it. Use explanatory figures and references beside the claims. Follow with detailed coverage of the relevant areas; put reference-search/snowballing methods near the bottom, and agents, review rounds, model provenance and process details last. Keep qualifications next to affected scientific claims, without replacing the findings with a process-status preamble. A plan explains the research questions, why they matter, the approach and the expected result in ordinary language. Explicitly register and link the results; a plan or machine receipt is not the result. Verify the rendered report and finish recoverable independent-review work before closing; an unresolved tooling defect is work to resolve, not a reason to declare the requested research finished. This is John's correction after his first serious review of the literature output, not optional styling.
119 
120 **Apply corrections before dependent review (2026-09-08).** Read an independent review's actual findings and apply the required changes before freezing or launching its downstream correction check. A completed output file alone is not a signal that the artifact is ready for final review. If a report changes after a review snapshot, verify the changed claims explicitly; never imply that the earlier receipt covers them. In structured model calls, put the human summary inside the requested JSON field and require one complete JSON object without a prose preface.

122 ### Invocation discipline — ZERO deliberation at start (added 2026-07-11; this is why John keeps having to remind)
123 
124 When a foundry skill is invoked, the operating parameters below are **ALREADY DECIDED**. Do NOT open an internal
125 discussion about whether/how to do them, do NOT ask John, do NOT re-derive them each run — just DO them. Spending
126 the first moves of a run debating "how do I do the 5:1 / Heavy" is the exact failure mode this rule kills.
127 
128 1. **Assess complexity/model use upfront.** Apply the existing depth/stakes rules, resolve current selected families and latest/highest capabilities, and record the actual seat. Do not recreate a second tier table or ask a ritual model-choice question.
129 2. **Independent review is stakes-gated and family-aware.** Use the configured independent family when the gate fires, and stamp same-family/absent checks honestly. Gemini uses agy-dispatch only when selected and its capability contract is verified; no bare Gemini or API-key fallback.
130 3. **The ~10-minute status update is automatic** — emitted on your own initiative during any long foundry/trio
131    run, WITHOUT John asking. The format is NOT defined here: use the **LOCKED Status-table format** in the
132    user-global `AGENTS.md` (`C:\Users\example\.claude\AGENTS.md` → "Long-run progress updates — the 10-minute
133    rule", locked by John 2026-07-01: `[HH:MM]` header, bordered field block, Effort/Doing/Status/Tests/Blocker/
134    Procs, ETA + To-do footer, chat window as primary channel, cadence armed AT LAUNCH). A 2026-07-11 session
135    drafted a second format here unaware of the locked one; the global table WINS — one standard, defined once.
136    A long-running skill that goes silent is a defect.

138 ### Run capture for training — EVERY job leaves a machine-readable record (added 2026-07-11, John's directive)
139 
140 Every foundry/trio skill run captures its work in TWO layers under the skill's `journal/`:
141 
142 1. **The human entry (unchanged):** the curated `NNNN-<slug>.md` — 7 fields, ≤15 lines, one per real run.
143    Id = **max(existing NNNN)+1 over the WHOLE directory** — never read the low numbers as the frontier
144    (gandalf accumulated 32 colliding ids that way; journal 0299).
145    This layer stays HUMAN-ONLY: no machine dumps in the `NNNN` namespace, ever (the Gandalf journal drowned
146    under 460 auto-dumped files and its sleep-loop signal died — that is the failure mode this split prevents).
147 2. **The training record (NEW, required):** `journal/runs/<UTC-timestamp>-<runid>.json` — machine-readable,
148    committed, written by the ENGINE where one exists (Foreman run-live, Crucible, researchPrime rounds, Gandalf
149    host, Jumper CLI) and by the operating agent for prompt-only skills. Schema (keep flat, keep small):
150    `{ skill, tier, started, ended, input, params, output, result, cross_model, models, duration_s, journal_ref }`
151    where `input` = the task/prompt (or a path pointer when large), `params` = the decisive knobs (stakes, fanOut,
152    roundCap, wave range…), `output` = pointer(s) to the deliverable(s), `result` = the honest outcome
153    (verdict/grade/GO-HALT/converged + one-line note), `journal_ref` = the NNNN entry it pairs with.
154    Large payloads go NEXT TO the record as files in the same `runs/` dir, pointed to — never inlined.
155    A crash storm collapses to ONE aggregated record. These records are the Foundry's TRAINING FEED
156    (sleep-loop distillation, few-shot exemplars, regression corpora) — they only have value if they are
157    written EVERY run, so an engine that finishes a job without its run record is a defect.

[Evidence, causal limits and candidate acceptance checks](skills/chekhov/planning/foundry-20260910-readiness/PROCESS-REVIEW.md) and paired Chekhov journal0026 are the current formal improvement intake for Foundry commissioning, Crucible plan review and Foreman/root supervision.
